topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes and outlines the learning objectives for cancer cell transformation and genetics.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and experimental cell transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanistic actions of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the functional categories and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors, using key regulators like Rb and p53 as examples.

topics.label: Forms and mechanisms of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific defects in DNA repair machinery, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise somatic mutation accumulation and inherited germline mutations drive cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with recommended reading and a preview of the next lecture.
